I have farmed these 7 mu for 30 years. I never went to school, but I know my land. I watch Old Wang across the road and my cousin — if their crops look good, I copy them.

Last year I put wheat on 5 mu, then maize after it, and peanut on 2 mu. This year I will do the same. My son works in the city and sends some money, but fertilizer is expensive now. Still, I would rather put a little too much than too little. If the harvest fails, my family has no food. Wasting some fertilizer is just money; losing the yield is a disaster.

For wheat: I buy the improved seed from the county shop — the same kind Li Sao bought last year in the red bag. I do not use old seed, it does not grow strong. Before planting in October, I spread one full 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer on each mu and rotary till it in. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I spread 20 kilograms of urea on top. That is what I did last year and I got about 450 kilograms per mu. I irrigate three times: once in winter if the ground is dry, once when the wheat is jointing, and once at filling. I spray pesticide twice, when I see aphids and then later for disease. 

For maize: After we cut the wheat in June, I plant hybrid maize seed. I buy new hybrid seed every year — saved maize seed does not grow well, I learned that the hard way. I have no time to plough deep because the summer season is short, so I plant no-tillage right into the wheat stubble. I put one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer in the row when planting, then at the big leaf stage I put 25 kilograms of urea. I irrigate three times: right after planting, at jointing, and when the tassel comes out. Two pesticide sprays — one for weeds at the start, one for worms later.

For peanut: I plant 2 mu with my own saved seed, the big pink peanuts my family has kept for years. I plough the land and make ridges. Each mu gets 25 kilograms of compound fertilizer — half a bag. My mother-in-law always said peanut does not need as much as corn, or it grows leaves and no pods. I irrigate twice: at flowering and when the pods are fattening. Two pesticide sprays for bugs and leaf spot. At harvest I hire my nephew for two days to help dig, I pay him 100 yuan a day.
